content: Rabeprazole is prescribed to treat conditions where the stomach produces excessive acid. These conditions include ulcers, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Additionally, rabeprazole is used in combination with other medications to eradicate Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori), a bacterium that causes ulcers. Rabeprazole belongs to a class of medications known as proton-pump inhibitors, which work by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Rabeprazole is available as a delayed-release tablet, which is taken orally. It is typically taken once daily for a duration of 4 to 8 weeks, although it may be prescribed for longer periods in some cases. When used to treat ulcers, it should be taken after the morning meal. If prescribed in combination with other medications to eliminate H. pylori, it is taken twice daily, with the morning and evening meals, for 7 days. It is important to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take rabeprazole exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Swallow the tablets whole; do not split, chew, or crush them. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information if needed. Before taking rabeprazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to rabeprazole, lansoprazole (Prevacid), omeprazole (Prilosec), pantoprazole (Protonix), or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking. Be sure to mention medications such as cyclosporine (Neoral, Sandimmune), digoxin (Lanoxin), and ketoconazole (Nizoral), as your doctor may need to adjust the doses or monitor you for potential side effects. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have or have ever had liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking rabeprazole, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking rabeprazole. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Rabeprazole may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they are severe or persistent: headache, upset stomach, diarrhea, stomach pain, vomiting, constipation, dry mouth, changes in appetite (increased or decreased), muscle or bone pain, drowsiness, dizziness, or difficulty falling or staying asleep. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Store rabeprazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have any questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
